title: Choose the visual world for the planner console
question: Your inspiration is pinned: dark ground, one high-chroma accent, four panes, both themes toggleable. The roll assigned the Permit Board. A challenger beat it on both axes. Pick the world.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: The console is a measuring instrument, not a dashboard. Confidence is a trace read against an etched graticule, and the auto-apply threshold is a trigger level: below it the row rolls free, above it locks still. Refuses the card-grid dashboard your category always ships.
options.viewport: Icon rail left. Tree panel with search, work fronts carrying live counts. Centre: the queue, every row measured against a shared graticule so confidence is a position rather than a number to parse. Right rail: the live call panel, a trace that writes as the agent confirms each item. Threshold sits on a detented control, and moving it visibly locks or frees rows.
options.risk: Instrument metaphors go costume fast. If the graticule is decoration rather than a scale you actually read against, this becomes a skin. The graticule has to carry real measurement or it comes out.
options.case: Wins audience identification: this audience's colleagues sit in front of instrument panels all shift. Wins product clarity: trigger level is threshold and margin, two channels in one graticule is planned against actual on one axis, amber is already the warning semantic.

raised.raise: One absolute selection treatment, unmistakable from across a desk, rather than a subtle row tint. Borrowed from inversion-as-selection, not from the four greens.
Queue rank is a continuous visual property, legible without reading a label, not just a sort order.
The accent colour and the interactive affordance are the same thing. Accent-coloured means actionable; nothing decorative wears it.
Status colour is causal, not annotative: the colour says what will happen to the row, not merely what it is.

options.label: Permit Board
options.lineage: permit-to-work board, enamel tags on pegs
options.thesis: The six statuses become physical enamel tags hung on a shift board. State is a tag you can see from the far side of the room, and clearing the queue is taking tags down.
options.viewport: The queue as a board of hung tags, colour-coded by status, grouped by work front. Confidence is how firmly the tag is seated. The right rail is the shift log.
options.risk: Enamel and hi-vis is a narrow palette that fights a dark theme, and your pinned brief wants dark. Translating it means losing most of what makes an enamel tag read as enamel.
options.case: Strong audience identification, this is literally on their site. Weaker product clarity: a tag says state well and says confidence and margin badly.

options.label: Course Over Terrain
options.lineage: orienteering map and legend, ISOM inks
options.thesis: The schedule is fixed terrain in a colour language you learn once. The planner's queue is the course riding above it, control to control, and the course layer never edits the terrain.
options.viewport: The WBS as terrain, the queue as a numbered purple course over it. Each item pairs a marker with a coded description row. Punched controls check off.
options.risk: Its whole strength is a light map ground, which fights the pinned dark brief. Six ISOM inks also collide with the reserved six-status vocabulary.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright: the course layer never editing the terrain IS the staging-table safety property, and a control paired with a coded row IS a queue item. Loses audience identification, orienteering is not their world.

declined.label: Game Boy Four-Shade Field
declined.kept: One absolute selection treatment, unmistakable at a glance.
declined.reason: Four tones cannot carry six statuses plus a confidence ramp, and one font size removes hierarchy.

declined.label: Cracktro Scroller Queue
declined.kept: Rank as a continuous visual property rather than a badge.
declined.reason: No enclosure ever removes the row boundary a dense queue needs, and drift is motion on data.

declined.label: Drawcord Transforming Cape
declined.kept: The accent colour and the interactive affordance are one thing.
declined.reason: A transformation metaphor carries disclosure but not six statuses, confidence or density.

declined.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
declined.kept: Status colour is causal, not annotative.
declined.reason: Bending baselines destroys scanability in a dense operator queue.

canonCard.label: Dark Product Dashboard
canonCard.lineage: your reference, executed at full fidelity
canonCard.thesis: Exactly the image you attached: near-black ground, elevated rounded cards, one high-chroma accent, four panes, categorical tag chips. No irony, no smuggled quirk.
canonCard.viewport: Icon rail, tree sidebar with search, main work area, right activity feed. Cards, chips, avatar clusters.
canonCard.risk: Near-black with one neon accent is named in Impeccable's own calibration list as one of three looks AI interfaces cluster into. For SIH judging, this is the rendition most likely to invite the question you least want.
